CAUSE: B691 cloned an unbacked enum only when some variant has a payload, reasoning that a payload-less one is only replaced whole; but a whole write through a view IS `__replace`, an in-place assignment into the array every copy shares. WIDER than filed: every sharing seam moved the copy (let, assignment, struct field init, field read out, list element, return, closure capture, `mut` capture, destructure, a `mut` parameter whose write reached the caller's argument) under every in-place writer (`&mut` parameter, direct and generic `&mut self`, generic `&mut T`). FIX, door (a): every enum whose JS value is a mutable array is copied (`is_cloneable_aggregate`'s enum arm is `!enum_lowers_to_js_primitive`). MEASURED: no golden moved, `examples/todo` byte-identical, kolt's client +33 `__clone(` and +297 bytes of 4.58 MB, its server +11; nothing newly refused. Twelve pins in `borrows.rs` (ten seam pins red with the old predicate) and a native differential probe, identical on both backends. Enums with payloads written whole were already right (pinned). DOOR (b), measured and NOT built: a payload-less enum as a scalar `(base, key)` view removes the copies and newly refuses nothing in the estate today, but changes the language (`k == Plain::X` over `k: &Plain` would need `*k`): an owner question, carried in M193's notes together with the constraint B748 puts on M193 (a binding 'never written in place' must count `&mut` writes to ANY sharer).
